review: PR50 independent affected recheck: explaining/right third revision
scope: Visual inspection of the canonical PNG and this revision only, checked against the previous character-review findings. No asset edits or implementation.
approval_status: Reviewer assessment only; no human or art-owner approval is asserted.

reference.limitation: The canonical image is small; subtle eye/muzzle geometry remains a medium-confidence comparison. Its visible tooth treatment, clothing color blocks, and plain shoe design remain usable constraints.

decision: The explaining/right pose is readable and the image plausibly depicts the same character. It does not demonstrate that the previous identity and cutout defects are resolved. Do not use it as a production master or as the identity reference for a wider pose set.

affected_findings.observation: The visible upper teeth are still broad rounded beads/scallops, including the prominent central teeth. They have not returned to the canonical smaller, sharper scalloped/triangular treatment. The prompt's request for pointed teeth is not reflected convincingly in the actual image.
affected_findings.required_change: Restore the canonical dentition and preserve the original mouth outline before production acceptance.

affected_findings.observation: The eyes remain round, open, and visually dominant; the muzzle remains broad and blunt, similar to the earlier generated interpretation. I do not see a decisive return toward the canonical face. The overall palette and facial landmarks still make the identity plausible, but strict face preservation is unproven.
affected_findings.required_change: Use a character-controlled source or an illustrator-approved face model, then compare at matched display height rather than accepting prompt wording as evidence.

affected_findings.observation: The shoe sides shown here are plain; the previously added double side stripes are absent. Dark uppers, pale soles, and light lace bars are broadly consistent with the canonical shoes.
affected_findings.qualification: This passes the visible stripe issue in this image; it does not certify hidden surfaces or other candidates.

affected_findings.observation: Visible cyan/blue fringe persists around the head and body. Detached cyan fragments are apparent along the viewer-left shoulder/torso silhouette; warm yellow/red fringe remains around hands. A real transparent background is present, but the cutout is not visually clean.
affected_findings.qualification: Near-opaque interior alpha is not itself the rejection reason. Visible colored contamination and detached residue are the defects; the far larger low-alpha bounds support the need to inspect these explicitly.
affected_findings.required_change: Clean actual edge contamination and isolated residue, preserve antialiasing, and inspect the final export on white, dark, and saturated backgrounds.

affected_findings.observation: The extended presenting arm, lowered opposite arm, and planted feet form a readable explanation pose. No obvious impossible elbow or duplicated limb is visible. The presenting hand's finger grouping is simplified; inspect its digit count and separations at final display size. The fine fabric texture and bright polished head remain more detailed than the source, without a new broad rendering style.

recommended_disposition.active_character: Keep the canonical mascot alone active.
recommended_disposition.candidate_use: Retain this genuine new artwork in a clearly labeled review-only candidate gallery with the unresolved defects disclosed.
recommended_disposition.production: Block mass production of the larger pose library until identity and cutout quality are controlled.
recommended_disposition.handoff: Prepare an illustrator/rig handoff containing the canonical source, explicit facial and clothing constraints, the reviewed pose directions, and these concrete defects. A stable character model or controlled illustration workflow is more defensible than multiplying the current inconsistent face interpretation.
recommended_disposition.final_gate: A separate audit of actual final stamped/exported assets remains required after corrections.
